players.product: optical fiber, fiber cable, and connectivity solutions for AI data center scale-out and scale-up networks; solar polysilicon, wafers, and modules

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (call): year over year, sales grew 14% to a record $4.41 billion and EPS grew 26% to $0.72; operating margin expanded 170 basis points to 20.2%, hitting the SpringBoard 20% target a full year early; ROIC up 150 basis points to 14.2%; free cash flow $732 million. Full year 2025: sales grew 13% to a record $16.4 billion, EPS grew 29% to $2.52, operating margin 19.3%, free cash flow $1.7 billion. CFO: from here it is 'highly likely that our operating margin goes above 20%', but no new margin target is being set.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $4.41 billion (+14%); EPS $0.72 (+26%); operating margin 20.2%; ROIC 14.2%; free cash flow $732 million; FY2025 sales $16.4 billion (+13%), EPS $2.52 (+29%)

quarterly_data.signal: Optical Communications Q4 2025: sales $1.7 billion, up 24% year over year; net income $305 million, up 57%; net income margin 18%. Full-year optical net income was $1 billion, up 71%. CFO: 'The majority of growth in optical was driven by the outstanding adoption of our new GenAI products', and the segment is expected to continue to drive significant growth, with the Meta announcement cited as a proof point.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical Q4 sales $1.7 billion (+24%); net income $305 million (+57%); net income margin 18%; FY2025 optical net income $1 billion (+71%)

quarterly_data.signal: Inside-the-data-center (enterprise) mix: for full year 2025 the enterprise business grew 61% year over year and the hyperscale data center portion grew significantly faster. CEO: enterprise was about $3 billion for the year, 'Roughly two-thirds of that would be the hyperscalers, of which Meta was one.' CFO: a little over $3 billion in enterprise; enterprise in total grew 60% and the hyperscale portion grew almost double that rate in 2025. Direct hyperscaler sales (such as Meta) are booked in enterprise; sales to carriers are booked in carrier.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise +61% (FY2025); enterprise about $3 billion; roughly two-thirds hyperscalers; hyperscale portion grew almost double the enterprise rate

quarterly_data.signal: Carrier Networks grew 15% in full year 2025, primarily from sales to interconnect data centers. CFO: long-haul data center interconnect has so far gone through carriers ('our customers, for example, Lumen, are building out networks for data centers'), which sits in the carrier business. He expects carrier to grow over the next several years, with fiber-to-the-home also growing, but 'probably the largest driver is data center interconnect.'
quarterly_data.figure: carrier +15% (FY2025); majority of growth from data center interconnect

quarterly_data.signal: Supply/pricing color: CEO said that 'on a generic basis... there is enough fiber in the world to meet demand', but the capacity expansions are for Corning's new high-density fiber, cable and connectivity products, where demand is 'very, very robust' and 'If we could make more of these new products, we could sell more.' These products give customers better, more reliable optical performance 'in about half the space with significantly reduced installation cost'. He expects some of that value creation to end up accruing to shareholders as Corning begins to master manufacturing of these product sets, so profitability should improve over time. He added that the new products are increasing demand for Corning's products relative to others' products.

Hyperscaler long-term agreements beyond Meta: Corning is 'concluding similar long-term agreements with other major customers to dedicate capacity for them as well'. CEO: 'They are of a similar size and scale, each of them, to the Meta agreement', and there are 'several of them'. They are not yet fully included in the upgraded SpringBoard plan because not all have been concluded, and because the dedicated capacity is still being built, 'we won't see the financial impact really until you get into '27, and then it will continue to build to 2028.' The structures share cost and risk through customer prepayments and stringent long-term customer commitments, modelled on the display 'Gen ten and a half' agreements and Apple's $2.5 billion cover-glass commitment.
quarterly_data.figure: each similar in size and scale to the up to $6 billion Meta agreement; financial impact from '27, building to 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up optics timing (CEO, answering a CPO/scale-up question): 'we do not have a significant revenue amount for scale-up included in this most recent SpringBoard upgrade', so it would be on top. Photons use 'greater than three times lower power' than electrons even over very short links, and the advantage 'can be 20 times or more' at longer reach or higher bit rate. There is a broad effort to bring optics into scale-up, closer to the GPUs and switch ASICs; he believes those links going to photons, with Corning's innovations playing a significant role, is inevitable. On timing, some scenarios fall between now and 2028 and others start 'primarily starting immediately in 2028 and beyond', so the plan treats timing conservatively.
quarterly_data.figure: no significant scale-up revenue in the upgraded plan; photons greater than three times lower power, 20 times or more at longer reach/higher bit rate; timing between now and 2028 or 2028 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: SpringBoard upgrade (first announced on this call): the internal plan now adds $11 billion in incremental annualized sales by 2028, up from the original $8 billion, taking the annualized run rate from $13.1 billion at the Q4 2023 start to $24 billion by 2028. For 2026, the internal plan now adds $6.5 billion (from $6 billion) and the high-confidence plan now adds $5.75 billion (from $4 billion). Corning has added $4.6 billion of incremental annualized sales since launch, hitting the upgraded high-confidence target a year early. Management cited optical communications and the Meta agreement as key parts of the upgrade.
quarterly_data.figure: $11 billion incremental annualized sales by 2028 (from $8 billion); $24 billion run rate by 2028; 2026: internal $6.5 billion, high-confidence $5.75 billion; $4.6 billion added so far

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance and capex: for Q1 2026, Corning expects sales to grow approximately 15% year over year to $4.2 billion to $4.3 billion and EPS to grow about 26% to $0.66 to $0.70, including a temporary solar-ramp drag of approximately $0.03 to $0.05. For full year 2026, capex is expected to be about $1.7 billion, a few hundred million above depreciation (around the $1.3 billion level), with 'optical... a place... where we'll direct a lot of that capital'. The CFO confirmed that 'some of the capital we plan to spend in 2026' is for the Meta deal. The capex figure already builds in the customer agreements management expects to complete, and customer upfront payments may offset capital or show up in operating cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 sales $4.2 billion to $4.3 billion (approximately 15%); EPS $0.66 to $0.70 (about 26%); FY2026 capex about $1.7 billion; depreciation around $1.3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Solar (Hemlock and Emerging Growth businesses): Q4 sales were $526 million, up 62%, driven by growth in polysilicon and module sales for the solar industry; Q4 net income was $1 million, down year over year, mainly because of the cost of ramping capacity for polysilicon, wafers and modules. The Q4 drag was sized at about $0.03 and ended a little higher. Corning still plans to build solar into a $2.5 billion revenue stream by 2028, with margins at or above the Corning average.
quarterly_data.figure: Hemlock and Emerging Growth Q4 sales $526 million (+62%); Q4 net income $1 million; solar target $2.5 billion revenue by 2028

connects_to.relationship: multiyear up to $6 billion agreement for optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions supporting AI and apps infrastructure

contracts.signal: Original announcement discussed on the call: 'Just yesterday, we announced that Corning Incorporated and Meta announced a multiyear, up to $6 billion agreement' to support Meta's apps, technologies and AI ambitions using Corning's newest optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions. 'Meta will serve as the anchor customer for the expansion and upgrading our manufacturing and technology capabilities across our operations in North Carolina.' The deal is structured with customer prepayments and stringent long-term commitments for revenue assurance. It will be booked entirely in enterprise ('the Meta deal would be all in enterprise'), and 'some of the capital we plan to spend in 2026' is for the Meta deal.
contracts.date_signed: announced the day before this call ('Just yesterday')
contracts.type: multiyear supply agreement (anchor customer for North Carolina capacity expansion)
